title: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo: Notorious Mexican drug lord dies at 80 | CNN
text:
Lee este artículo en español.

Source: CNN

Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, a founder of the first major drug cartel in Mexico, died on Sunday at the age of 80 in a hospital in Guadalajara, Jalisco.

As one of the leaders of the Guadalajara Cartel, the so-called “boss of bosses” laid the foundations for large-scale drug trafficking in the country and helped transform cocaine routes to the United States.

Félix Gallardo had been convicted over the kidnapping, torture and death of US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) agentEnrique “Kiki” Camarenain 1985, a crime that caused a diplomatic crisis between Mexico and Washington.

Local security authorities reported that the former cartel leader died due to multiple organ failure after several years of health problems. He had been transferred to the hospital from the Puente Grande maximum security prison, where he had been held since 2015.

Rising to prominence in the 1970s, Félix Gallardo ignited a series of turf wars that have led to hundreds of thousands of deaths and disappearances in ensuing decades, according to Reuters.

Félix Gallardo began his working life in public security, according to Mexican journalist José Reveles, a specialist in drug trafficking issues.

“He was a policeman. He was in charge of the security of the then-governor of Sinaloa, Leopoldo Sánchez Celis, when he was very young,” Reveles told CNN.

During those years, Félix Gallardo and other police leaders gradually became involved in drug trafficking using their knowledge of the terrain along with repressive tactics, Reveles added.

He co-founded and led the Guadalajara Cartel withRafael Caro Quinteroand Ernesto Fonseca Carrillo in the 1970s, according to the US State Department.

At that time, he worked with various traffickers, including Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, who became part of the Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s.

Félix Gallardo became known as the “boss of bosses” for being one of the wealthiest and most recognized Mexican drug lords of the 20th century.

Reveles explained that he gained that prominence largely because he was the first to establish connections with Colombians to ship cocaine to the United States.

“He had amassed a considerable fortune when he was apprehended in 1989,” Reveles said. “Some 50 houses, residences, several ranches, and cash were seized from him. At that time, they estimated it at around $500 million.”

Following his 1989 arrest, Félix Gallardo was sentenced to 40 years in prison on drug-trafficking and weapons charges tied to the Guadalajara Cartel, according to Reuters.

The cartel subsequently dealt with internal conflicts andsplitinto four factions: the Sinaloa Cartel, the Tijuana Cartel, the Juárez Cartel and the Sonora Cartel.

While incarcerated, Félix Gallardo faced a separate prosecution over the kidnapping, torture and murder of DEA agent Camarena and Mexican pilot Alfredo Zavala Avelar in 1985.

In 2017, he received another sentence of 37 years for Camarena’s murder, Reveles said.

Reveles added that the drug lords of that era no longer have a tangible influence today, and that their names have more power as part of the history of drug trafficking: “They are now history, particularly him, Félix Gallardo.”

Fonseca Carrillo has been under house arrest for five years, and Caro Quintero was recently recaptured after being free for nine years.

“The three big bosses of that era are now neutralized; the Guadalajara Cartel no longer exists as such,” Reveles said.

Even so, Félix Gallardo can still be considered one of the founders of modern drug trafficking, the Mexican journalist added, because prior to the arrival of the Guadalajara Cartel, Mexico was not a “stepping stone” for drugs to other countries.

“The Guadalajara Cartel opened the door for cocaine to enter Mexico en route to the United States, and we’re talking about hundreds of tons of a multibillion-dollar business that continues to this day … You can’t talk about criminal groups involved in drug trafficking without mentioning Guadalajara. Guadalajara is historic. That’s its role,” he concluded.
